title: Fuzzycomplete
subtitle: Fuzzy SQL completion with a catalog-aware matcher
intro: Suggest SQL keywords and catalog names from a partial query using a fuzzy matcher. Loading it replaces the CLI’s preloaded stock autocomplete; inspect suggestions directly through the table function.

reference.name: sql_auto_complete(query)
reference.description: Table function: suggest completions for partial SQL text.

reference.name: suggestion
reference.description: Candidate text returned by the completion provider.

reference.name: suggestion_start
reference.description: Character offset at which the candidate should replace text.

reference.name: max_suggestion_count := 5
reference.description: Cap the number of suggestions; stock named parameters are accepted.

reference.name: Tab in the CLI
reference.description: Requests completion through the active provider.

reference.name: duckdb_extensions()
reference.description: Check whether autocomplete was already loaded.

reference.name: duckdb_functions()
reference.description: Inspect the registered completion function and its parameters.

notes.title: Check the active provider
notes.body: LOAD fuzzycomplete replaces an already loaded stock provider, so load it after startup or in ~/.duckdbrc. If you load both explicitly, load autocomplete first. Check with SLCT: the fuzzy matcher suggests SELECT. loaded = true alone does not identify the provider.

notes.title: Matcher and client are separate
notes.body: Fuzzy matching rewards ordered characters and word boundaries; ties favour SELECT and FROM, your own tables, and columns of tables in the statement. Comments are skipped. SQL calls inspect suggestions; they do not add an editor to other clients.

examples.title: Inspect the loaded provider
examples.sql:
SELECT extension_name, loaded
FROM duckdb_extensions()
WHERE extension_name IN
  ('autocomplete', 'fuzzycomplete');
examples.caption: Reports loaded extensions; use the suggestion check below to verify fuzzy behavior.

examples.title: Inspect SQL suggestions
examples.caption: A subsequence query confirms that the fuzzy provider is active.

examples.caption: The client must call DuckDB’s active completion provider for Tab.
examples.reason: Interactive Tab requires an editor/terminal session; SQL suggestion behavior is checked locally.

assertions: SELECT CASE WHEN count(*)=1 AND min(trim(suggestion))='SELECT' THEN true ELSE error('Fuzzy provider is not active') END FROM sql_auto_complete('SLCT');
